newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH INDMIN MOVES TO BLOCK 1996 UTILITY DIVIDENDS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH INDMIN MOVES TO BLOCK 1996 UTILITY DIVIDENDS.

text.p: The Czech Industry and Trade Ministry said on Tuesday that it would use its controlling stakes to block the payment of 1996 dividends of the country's 16 regional gas and electrical utilities.

Ministry spokeswoman Zuzana Fialova told Reuters the ministry was also working on a plan to block the main Czech power comany CEZ a.s. from paying its planned first-ever dividend on 1996 profits, but added that a final decision had not been taken.
"The companies need to gather maximum possible funds for their development needs," Fialova said.
"We have the interest to include CEZ into (the plan). It is being worked on, but a final decision has not been taken yet," she added.
CEZ is the most widely-held utility stock in the country and is the second most highly capitalised issue on the Prague Stock Exchange.
CEZ's board has said preliminarily that it would propose a dividend of roughly 30 to 35 crowns per share on 1996 earnings.

Fialova said that one of the reasons to block the 1996 dividends was that planned energy price hikes would be politically difficult in time when the distributors were paying out profits to shareholders.
Fialova said the plan was temporary and so far only included 1996 dividends.

She added that if the boards of the companies involved propose dividends at upcoming annual general meetings, the ministry or National Property Fund representatives will vote against the overall distribution of 1996 profits.
